name: Tetouan Medina
hero_subtitle: A UNESCO World Heritage treasure showcasing exceptional Andalusian-Moroccan heritage, white-washed alleys, and vibrant souks.

overview.title: A living masterpiece of Andalusian history
overview.p1: The Medina of Tetouan is remarkably intact, having served as the main point of contact between Andalusia and Morocco following the Reconquista in the 15th century. Rebuilt by Andalusian refugees, its unique architecture reflects a profound fusion of Moorish and Andalusian traditions.
overview.p2: Wandering through its labyrinth of white-washed streets reveals wrought-iron balconies, green-tiled roofs, hidden fountains, and bustling artisan quarters where centuries-old crafts are still practiced daily.
overview.p3: Take your time exploring the traditional souks, interacting with local craftsmen, and appreciating why this cultural gem earned its prestigious UNESCO World Heritage designation.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Tetouan Medina

1.title: Wear comfortable walking shoes
1.desc: The medina features stone-paved streets, inclines, and steps. Flat, sturdy footwear will make your exploration much more enjoyable.

2.title: Hire a local guide if needed
2.desc: While you can wander freely, an official local guide can help you navigate the intricate alleys and share fascinating historical anecdotes.

3.title: Respect local customs
3.desc: Ask permission before photographing local residents in their workshops, and dress modestly out of respect for local traditions.

q1.question: Is the Tetouan Medina free to visit?
q1.answer: Yes. Walking through the streets, gates, and open-air markets of the Medina is entirely free.

q2.question: How long do I need to explore?
q2.answer: 2 to 3 hours is generally sufficient for a comprehensive walk through the main commercial alleys and historic quarters.

q3.question: Can I visit without a guide?
q3.answer: Yes, many travelers explore independently, though a guide can enrich the experience by explaining the Andalusian history and heritage.
